observations: Photo 0 shows a large, dirty engine and gearbox assembly suspended by chains inside a shipping container. The engine has visible cylinder heads, intake manifold, and various hoses and components. The front of the engine has a black plastic cover with a label that is not legible. The assembly is covered in grime and sand, suggesting it has been stored or transported in rough conditions.

Photo 1 shows the same engine from a wider angle, still inside the container, with a man standing beside it. The engine appears to be the same unit, with similar components visible. The container floor is covered in sand or dirt. The watermark 'NZ JAPANESE AUTOS' is visible on both photos.
No visible branding, model numbers, or part numbers are readable on the engine or gearbox in either photo.
The engine appears to be a V6, based on the three visible cylinder head ports on each side, consistent with a 2GR-FE engine used in Toyota vehicles.
The gearbox is attached to the engine, and the assembly is being handled with chains, indicating it is heavy and likely complete.
